title: Jude and the Current
premise: Odile Winterbourne, a bush pilot who ferries medicine and secrets across the interior, is forced down by a storm near a coastal cave the tide has just exposed — a cave locals say holds the ledger of a vanished magistrate who once ruled the range with his own brand of justice. Inside she finds Jude, a boy raised by the cave's last keeper, carrying both the ledger and a price on his head from men who want that history erased. Hunted by the mining consortium's enforcers and racing the first snows, Odile and Jude cross the range to deliver the ledger to the one judge still honest enough to act on it. They arrive with the pass closing behind them, the enforcers dead or scattered, and Odile finally choosing to stop moving — because some things are worth standing still for.
about_author: J. M. Vasquez spent a decade flying supply runs in remote northern communities before turning to fiction, and their work carries the cadence of radio chatter and runway gravel. They live half the year off-grid, writing by lamplight and insisting that every good story begins with weather.

chapters.title: Freight and Rumors
chapters.summary: POV Odile. A routine medicine run into Kettle Landing turns strange when a passenger pays in gold dust and asks about a cave that appears twice a century. Odile's restlessness surfaces; she takes the fare because stopping costs more. Beat: unease disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Tide's Toll
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Forced down on the coast by an early storm, Odile shelters in a sea arch and watches the ebb reveal a cave mouth no chart admits exists. Against her better judgment, she goes in with a headlamp and a flare. Beat: curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Kept the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Deep inside, she finds Jude — fourteen, feral-polite, guarding a waterproof chest of records kept by generations of cave keepers. He tells her the magistrate wrote down every injustice the law refused to touch. Beat: wonder shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What the Magistrate Wrote
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Flashback through Jude's training: the old keeper teaching him to read entries, to copy them, to understand why memory itself was contraband. The keeper's recent death left Jude alone with the chest. Beat: grief braided into duty.

chapters.title: Engines in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Snowmobile engines echo up the beach — the consortium's enforcers have tracked her downed plane. She and Jude escape through a secondary passage as the tide begins its return. Beat: panic sharpening into partnership.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude refuses to hand over the ledger but offers a bargain: guide her over the range before snowfall if she flies him to Judge Amara Sorel, the last official who ever cited the ledger in a ruling. Beat: wary negotiation, first trust.

chapters.title: Kettle Landing Again
chapters.summary: POV Odile. They resupply in town under false names and learn the consortium has posted a reward describing Jude precisely. An old friend warns Odile she's already reported. Beat: betrayal, the cost of being known.

chapters.title: The Burned Homestead
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Passing his childhood valley, Jude finds the keeper's cabin torched and a consortium survey stake driven into the soil — they're erasing not just papers but ground. He takes a charred page as proof. Beat: rage finding purpose.

chapters.title: River of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: POV Odile. A river crossing goes wrong; their raft guide sells their route to the enforcers mid-crossing. Odile improvises a night run down rapids to lose them. Beat: adrenaline, and grudging respect between the two.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Cold Fork
chapters.summary: POV Jude. They shelter with a hermit who once served the magistrate and confirms the ledger's power: whole towns paid debts and settled feuds by it. But he also reveals the ledger contains an entry naming Odile's father. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Her Father's Page
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Reading the entry, Odile learns her father took consortium money to burn an earlier copy — and hanged himself after. Her lifelong running suddenly has an address. Beat: shame transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Whiteout at the Col
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The storm arrives early; they're pinned above the treeline with enforcers climbing behind. Jude's mountain craft saves them in a whiteout bivouac, but supplies are nearly gone. Beat: vulnerability, mutual dependence made explicit.

chapters.title: The Enforcer's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Enforcer captain Rell catches them alone and offers Jude a deal: surrender the ledger, live comfortably on consortium payroll. Jude counters by reading Rell's own family's grievances aloud from it. Beat: temptation met with the weapon of memory.

chapters.title: Rell's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Rell lets them go — for now — and Odile realizes the ledger corrupts as easily as it redeems: everyone wants to be its hero or its victim. She and Jude argue about whether such power should exist at all. Beat: thematic fault line opened.

chapters.title: Sawmill Town
chapters.summary: POV Jude. In a company town, they witness the present-day injustice the ledger would record: wages stolen, a strike broken. Jude is tempted to intervene directly; Odile argues justice delivered by a boy with a box isn't justice at all. Beat: idealism tested against pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Long Traverse
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Three days of high-country travel, told in quiet detail — frostbite checks, shared stories, Jude teaching Odile to read weather the way keepers read tides. The chase recedes; something like family forms. Beat: tenderness at altitude.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Timberline
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The consortium's second team, led by a man with no interest in deals, ambushes them. Odile crashes their escape sled deliberately to save Jude, breaking her wrist. Beat: sacrifice reversing their roles — now he carries her.

chapters.title: Descent into the Valley
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Injured and out of food, they descend toward the provincial seat as snow seals the passes behind them. There is no way back, no way around — only forward to Sorel's courthouse. Beat: grim determination, point of no return.

chapters.title: The Honest Judge
chapters.summary: POV Jude. They reach Judge Sorel, who is being pressured to recuse herself from the consortium's land case. Jude presents the ledger; she recognizes the risk and accepts custody anyway. Beat: hope arriving battered but intact.

chapters.title: Reading Into Record
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Rell's men attempt one last seizure at the courthouse steps; Odile, one-armed and furious, stalls them while Sorel enters the ledger into official record, making its contents public and untouchable. Beat: climax — courage against force, memory against money.

chapters.title: After the Snows
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Weeks later: hearings begin, the survey stakes come out, Rell testifies in exchange for amnesty. Jude, no longer needed as keeper, must decide who he is when the ledger belongs to everyone. Beat: release, and the strangeness of freedom.

chapters.title: Where Odile Lands
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Spring. Odile repairs her plane but doesn't sell it; instead she files a new route — medicine, mail, and copies of the public record to every settlement in the range. She stops moving, in the way that matters. Beat: resolution — justice institutionalized, wandering ended.
